100926: On November 21 2015, two Yelp IP addresses were reported to be exposing Uchiwa dashboards on port 8080. A hardcoded password was found on a Sensu check, which provided access to a RabbitMQ server running on the same machine. The issue was quickly fixed by updating firewall rules, and a full internal audit of all affected systems was conducted.
105991: The "remember me" token (`user_auth_token`) was generated even when the "Remember me" box at the login page was not checked, leading to a longer-lasting session than the user intended. The issue was that the session could be reestablished using the previously obtained `user_auth_token` even after the user had logged out, providing continued access to the account.
127620: The new Hacktivity view unintentionally disclosed metadata about non-public reports through the leakage of report IDs correlated with teams, researchers, and bounty/swag actions. This could have allowed outside parties to glean information about undisclosed reports if report IDs were mentioned in other contexts.
127844: The web authentication endpoint of the website had a vulnerability that allowed for brute-force attacks on user credentials. The endpoint only had rate-limiting based on IP, which could be easily bypassed using various methods such as using multiple IP addresses or botnets. This allowed attackers to make unlimited login attempts and potentially compromise user accounts.
139402: The endpoint at https://kb.informatica.com/_layouts/infa_kb/preview/EmailExtended.aspx?docid=anything was vulnerable. Unauthenticated emails could be sent through the endpoint, allowing impersonation and spoofing of any email address. The message body field also permitted HTML injection, enabling malicious links and images to be included in emails. An attacker exploited these vulnerabilities by sending a spoofed email with a convincing subject and embedded link to harvest user credentials.
152052: A vulnerability was found where an attacker could submit a cross-site request forgery to take over a user account on a website by changing the account name, email, type, and notification settings without confirming the user's password. The website was not requiring a confirmation token on account setting changes or asking for the password before applying changes. Passwords and tokens should be required to protect account settings from unauthorized modifications.
155774: A vulnerability was discovered in the Slack platform that allowed an attacker to bypass two-factor authentication (2FA) by exploiting a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability. By tricking a logged-in user into clicking a malicious link, the attacker could force the user to add a new mobile number for 2FA. The attacker would then receive the verification code and automatically verify it. This allowed the attacker to log in to the victim's account and bypass 2FA using the newly added mobile number.
165727: The Slack iOS app was found to be vulnerable to a rate-limit bypass issue. The "/api/auth.signin" endpoint lacked a rate-limit mechanism, allowing an attacker to brute-force the 2FA code without triggering any restrictions. This contrasted with the Slack web application, which implemented a rate-limit that prevented excessive 2FA attempts.
166265: The E-mail addresses registered on biz.yelp.com could be verified on the login and forgot password pages. This allowed attackers to determine which E-mail addresses were registered on the system, potentially facilitating further attacks.
167489: The vulnerability allowed an attacker to bypass the account closure mechanism and regain access to a closed account. The attacker could perform actions such as adding photos, sending friend requests, and sending invites, but could not perform restricted actions like writing reviews or sending messages.
170310: The blog post describes a technique to bypass the rate limiting on the /users/password endpoint of the HackerOne platform. The technique involves appending a null byte (%00) to the email parameter in the password reset request, which allows the user to bypass the rate limit and send multiple password reset requests. The report also mentions that a similar technique was attempted on the /users/sign_in endpoint, but it was not as successful.
174882: The vulnerability allowed a user to request a "ShowCheckIn Alert" for a non-friend user. This request was observed to be successful, despite the target user not being a friend of the requesting user.
